## Context / Problem

On an Apple-silicon macOS host without Rosetta, 17 reconciler tests fail on a clean tree because `pypandoc_binary` 1.17's `py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64` wheel bundles an **x86_64** pandoc. uv picked the right wheel; the wheel's contents are wrong. Upstream ([JessicaTegner/pypandoc#447](https://github.com/JessicaTegner/pypandoc/issues/447)) is open, unassigned, with no PR, and 1.17 is the newest release — so neither waiting nor re-pinning helps.

Reproduced in this worktree at `2fb6062bfe5`, no local changes: `pytest tests/unit/reconciler/test_wiki_render.py tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_cutover.py tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py -q` → **17 failed, 57 passed**, underlying `OSError: [Errno 86] Bad CPU type in executable`.

Two commits already landed for this defect class and left exactly one gap. `9af50584d0a` (`dc28-2807-5b1d-4da7`) documents a **manual** download + `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` export in `docs/local-dev-env.md:35-66`; `fda55e3655e` (`9119-3f7b-22c0-4421`) widened provenance verification to accept the native arm64 binary (`scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:65-72`). What is missing is making it **automatic**, so a freshly provisioned worktree is not born red.

## Approach

Repair the environment at **bootstrap**, triggered by an **architecture mismatch** rather than by a platform name or a CI provider.

`scripts/ensure_pandoc.py` reads the first 16 bytes of the pandoc that `pypandoc` bundles and decodes the executable's architecture from the Mach-O or ELF header. Measured on this host: the bundled binary's Mach-O header is `cffaedfe 07000001` (cputype `0x01000007` = `CPU_TYPE_X86_64`) while `platform.machine()` is `arm64`. When the decoded architecture matches the host, the script exits 0 having done nothing and having touched no network — which is every Linux and x86_64-macOS environment, including all CI cells. On a mismatch it downloads the pinned upstream release, verifies the **extracted binary's** SHA-256 against a hard-coded pin, and installs it to the repo-local, git-ignored `.tools/bin/pandoc`.

That shape is not invented here: `Makefile:467-482` (`actionlint-bin`) already installs a pinned, SHA-256-verified third-party binary into `.tools/bin` (`Makefile:51`, `.gitignore` `.tools/`). Reusing it adds no new mechanism *kind*, keeps the download out of `.venv` (where `uv sync` would overwrite it and corrupt the wheel's recorded hashes), and never touches `PATH`.

Selection at test time must use `PYPANDOC_PANDOC`, not `PATH`: pypandoc probes every candidate and keeps the **highest** version it can execute, so a Homebrew pandoc 3.11 would beat a 3.9 in `.venv/bin` and break the `pandoc 3.9` pin assertion. `docs/local-dev-env.md:35-66` already records this. So `tests/conftest.py` sets `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` to `.tools/bin/pandoc` when that file exists, the user has not set the variable, and the file's decoded architecture matches the host. When the file is absent the hook does nothing at all — no import, no stat beyond one `exists()` — so CI behaviour is bit-for-bit unchanged.

The riskiest assumption was that the upstream release binary is byte-identical to the digest the repo already accepts. I tested it first, before writing any code: downloading `https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/releases/download/3.9/pandoc-3.9-arm64-macOS.zip` and hashing the member `pandoc-3.9-arm64/bin/pandoc` yields `140353e19f2518a76aa144ce90a7afcb6f485ba94d0dbe069e77c805277908c3`, which is already present in `ACCEPTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256["darwin-arm64"]` at `scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:69`. `file` reports `Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64` and `--version` reports `pandoc 3.9`. A test asserts that membership so the fetched artifact can never drift away from what the provenance check accepts.

On a mismatch the script cannot repair, `make install` **fails loudly** with the manual recipe in the message. Silent degradation is the defect this ticket exists to remove: the alternative leaves a venv whose pandoc cannot run and produces 17 unexplained red tests.

## Scope

- `scripts/ensure_pandoc.py` — new. Mach-O/ELF architecture decoding, the pinned download table, digest-verified install into `.tools/bin`, and `repo_pandoc_for_host()` for the test-time lookup.
- `Makefile` — new `ensure-pandoc` target modelled on `actionlint-bin` (`Makefile:467-482`); `install` invokes it after `uv sync`.
- `tests/conftest.py` — set `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` from `.tools/bin/pandoc` when present and arch-matched. `_REPO_ROOT` already exists at `tests/conftest.py:115`.
- `tests/scripts/test_ensure_pandoc.py` — new regression tests.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — replace the manual-only prerequisite with the automatic path, keeping the manual steps as the offline fallback.
- `NOTICE` — record that the dev bootstrap may fetch the same pandoc 3.9 from `jgm/pandoc` releases. Nothing becomes vendored or redistributed; `.tools/` is git-ignored.

## Testing

In `tests/scripts/test_ensure_pandoc.py` (marker `scripts`):

- **Happy path, no-op branch:** with a synthetic Mach-O arm64 header on an `arm64` host, `ensure()` returns a "matches" outcome and never calls the injected downloader (injected as a function that raises, so a call is a hard failure).
- **Happy path, repair branch:** with a mismatched bundled binary and an injected downloader returning the real release bytes, `ensure()` writes `.tools/bin/pandoc`, makes it executable, and reports "repaired".
- **Failure path:** the injected downloader returns bytes whose digest does not match the pin — `ensure()` raises, and `.tools/bin/pandoc` does **not** exist afterwards. This is the one that matters: a silently-accepted bad download would reintroduce an unrunnable binary.
- **Edge paths:** `read_binary_arch` decodes Mach-O `cffaedfe 07000001` → `x86_64`, Mach-O `cffaedfe 0c000001` → `arm64`, ELF `e_machine` `0x3e` → `x86_64` and `0xb7` → `arm64`, and returns `None` for a short/unknown file (so an unrecognised format degrades to "no mismatch detected", never to a spurious download).
- **Empty/absent path:** `repo_pandoc_for_host()` returns `None` when `.tools/bin/pandoc` is absent and when it is present but its decoded architecture differs from the host — the two conditions that must keep CI a no-op.
- **Pin-drift guard:** the digest `ensure_pandoc.py` pins is a member of `ACCEPTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256["darwin-arm64"]` loaded from `scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py`, so the fetched binary and the provenance allowlist cannot drift apart.

No test performs a real download; the network boundary is injected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On this arm64 macOS host without Rosetta, `make install` in a freshly provisioned worktree leaves `.tools/bin/pandoc` reporting `Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64` and `pandoc 3.9`; checked by running `file` and `--version` on it.
- [ ] With no `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` exported and no manual intervention, `pytest tests/unit/reconciler/test_wiki_render.py tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_cutover.py tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py -q` reports **74 passed** on that host (it reports 17 failed, 57 passed today).
- [ ] `test_pypandoc_and_pandoc_versions_are_pinned` still asserts `pypandoc.__version__ == "1.17"` and `pandoc 3.9`, and still FAILS rather than skips when pandoc is absent or drifted; checked by deleting `.tools/bin/pandoc` and confirming the test fails, not skips.
- [ ] The trigger is architecture, not platform name or CI provider: `scripts/ensure_pandoc.py` exits 0 with no network access when the decoded architecture matches the host, and `tests/conftest.py` sets nothing when `.tools/bin/pandoc` is absent — both covered by the tests above, so a Linux or no-CI checkout is unaffected.
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test_ensure_pandoc.py` passes, including the bad-digest case that asserts nothing is installed.
- [ ] `make verify` from this worktree shows the 17 reconciler failures gone and no new failures: the only remaining failures on this hardware are the 22 `tests/scripts/test_observability_*` failures owned by `7f3d-ddc9-04d9-4861`, and no others. (The original "`make verify` exits 0" criterion is unreachable by this ticket alone — see the comment of 2026-10-27 — and is replaced by this one.)
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` and `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` both exit 0, and no file in `src/rebar` exceeds the 800-LOC cap.
